dhp306:1: He who declares that to have happened which happened not, goes to hell, and also he who having done a thing, says, “I did it not;”
dhp306:3: Both these men are the same after death; they are men of evil deeds in the next world.
dhp307:1: Many about whose neck hangs the yellow robe, are evildoers and uncontrolled;
dhp307:3: Evildoers by reason of their evil deeds, they are reborn in Hell.
dhp308:1: Better were it to swallow an iron ball, red-hot, like a flame of fire,
dhp308:3: Than that one who is corrupt and lacks self-control should live on the charity of the land.
dhp309:1: Four misfortunes befall the heedless man who runs after other men’s wives:
dhp309:3: First, he acquires demerit; secondly, he sleeps in discomfort; thirdly, he incurs blame; fourthly, he goes to Hell.
dhp310:1: Acquisition of demerit, an evil future state, brief pleasure for the frightened man and woman,
dhp310:3: Severe punishment inflicted by the king; – therefore a man should not run after another man’s wife.
dhp311:1: Even as a blade of grass awkwardly grasped cuts the hand,
dhp311:3: So the work of a monk, badly handled, drags down to Hell.
dhp312:1: A loose deed or a corrupt course
dhp312:3: Or dubious chastity, brings no great fruit.
dhp313:1: If there is aught to be done, one should do it, one should do it with all his might,
dhp313:2: For a lax wandering-ascetic but scatters dust the more.
dhp313:3: It were better that an evil deed were left undone.
dhp314:1: It were better that an evil deed were left undone, for an evil deed causes suffering afterwards;
dhp314:3: It were better to do a good deed, for after doing a good deed, one does not suffer.
dhp315:1: Even as a frontier city is well guarded both within and without,
dhp315:3: Even so one should guard himself; let not a moment slip.
dhp315:5: For they that let the moments slip, mourn, delivered over to Hell.
dhp316:1: They that feel shame when they ought not to feel shame,
dhp316:2: And they that do not feel shame when they ought to feel shame,
dhp316:3: Such men, since they have embraced false views, go to an evil future state.
dhp317:1: They that see something to fear where no fear is,
dhp317:3: Such men, since they have embraced false views, go to an evil future state.
dhp318:1: They that see sin where no sin is, and they that see no sin where sin exists,
dhp318:3: Such men, since they have embraced false views, go to an evil future state.
dhp319:1: They who know sin in its sinfulness, and that which is harmless in its harmlessness,
dhp319:3: Such men, since they have embraced correct views, go to a happy future state.
